intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Walk the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a swim among the rock formations.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided tour of local Algarve wineries in the Lagoa wine region, sampling regional varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco. Visit 2-3 boutique quintas, learn about the unique terroir of southern Portugal, and enjoy paired local cheeses and charcuterie with your tastings.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the most photographed sea caves in the world. A guided 2-hour kayak excursion takes you through hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and secluded beaches accessible only by water, combining adventure with breathtaking coastal scenery.

experiences.name: Tavira Old Town & Seafood Culinary Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the charming historic streets of Tavira, one of the Algarve's most beautiful towns, stopping at local tascos and markets to sample traditional Algarvian dishes including cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), grilled sardines, and local pastries. A self-guided food walk with a recommended stop list.

experiences.name: Sunset Dolphin Watching Cruise with Wine
experiences.description: Set sail from Portimão on a 2-hour sunset cruise along the Algarve coastline in search of common and bottlenose dolphins. The boat provides a curated selection of local Algarve wines and sparkling vinho verde to enjoy as the sun dips below the Atlantic horizon, combining wildlife, scenery, and wine in one unforgettable experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, grab a coffee at the airport café, and arrange transfer to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa (approx. 45–60 min by bus/taxi or shared shuttle).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a short walk down to Praia da Marinha — one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches, famous for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear water. Explore the cliff-top walking path and enjoy the stunning views. Take a refreshing swim if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearby village of Carvoeiro (5 min by car or 25 min walk) for a relaxed first evening. Explore the small promenade and watch the sunset over the Atlantic from the cliff boardwalk.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at Faro Airport café (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Grab a bifana (pork sandwich) or tostas at a local café near the airport or en route (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — affordable local Portuguese dishes; try grilled sardines or cataplana for €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book shared airport transfer in advance to save money (€15–20 vs €50+ for private taxi). September is still warm (~26°C) with calm seas — perfect beach weather. Sunscreen and water are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk along the Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) — one of Portugal's most scenic coastal walks. The trailhead is near Praia da Marinha. The 6 km round-trip trail passes hidden sea caves, dramatic arches, and secluded beaches. Free and unmissable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Praia da Marinha for an afternoon of swimming and snorkeling among the sea caves and rock formations. The water is exceptionally clear here. Rent a kayak locally (€10–15/hour) to explore the sea grottos from the water level.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lagoa town center (10 min by bus) for a taste of authentic local life. Visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — one of the Algarve's oldest wine cooperatives — for an affordable wine tasting session featuring local Algarve wines (€5–10 for a tasting flight).

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria near the hotel — galão (milky coffee) and a pastel de nata (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local mini-market: bread, local cheese, chouriço, fruit, and a bottle of water (€5–7 total)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Lagoa — a no-frills local tasca with daily specials (prato do dia) for €8–10 including bread, soup, main, and a glass of house wine

day_by_day.notes: Start the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail early (before 9am) to avoid crowds and midday heat. Wear proper shoes — some sections are rocky. The trail is free but carry water. Adega de Lagoa may require a short reservation — call ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to Portimão (30 min, ~€2.50) and explore the city's vibrant Mercado Municipal de Portimão. Browse fresh produce, local cheeses, smoked meats, and Algarve almonds. A great place to stock up on affordable snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Praia da Rocha — Portimão's famous beach with golden sands and impressive sandstone rock formations. Spend the afternoon swimming and sunbathing. Explore the old fort (Fortaleza de Santa Catarina) at the eastern end of the beach — free entry, great panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner along the riverside Largo 1° de Dezembro — famous for its open-air sardine grills. This is one of the best and most affordable places in the Algarve to eat freshly grilled sardines straight off the charcoal grill.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a local café near Praia da Marinha (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Fresh snacks from Portimão market — olives, local bread, cheese (€5–6)
meals.dinner: Riverside sardine grill in Portimão — grilled sardines with bread and salad for €8–12 per person; pair with a cold Sagres beer

day_by_day.notes: Bus from Carvoeiro/Praia da Marinha area to Portimão runs regularly. Check Vamus Algarve bus schedules. Portimão is also known for its Formula 1 circuit — motorsport fans can visit the Autódromo Internacional do Algarve nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve (20 min by train from Tunes/Portimão or local bus). Visit the magnificent Castelo de Silves, a well-preserved red sandstone Moorish castle with sweeping views over orange groves and the Arade River. Entry €2.80 with discounts available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town on foot — walk the ancient city walls, visit the Gothic Sé Catedral de Silves (€1.30 entry), and wander the charming cobblestone streets. Stop at the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (€2 entry) to learn about the region's Moorish history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Lagoa area. Visit Quinta dos Vales — a family-run winery near Estômbar offering budget-friendly wine tastings and vineyard tours (€10–15 per person). September is harvest season — you may witness the grape harvest in action!

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at the hotel or local café (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Cervejaria Ponte Romana in Silves — affordable local lunch menu (prato do dia) for €8–10 with river views
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the hotel or pick up fresh bread, local presunto (cured ham), and Algarve wine from a supermarket for a budget evening picnic (€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: September is harvest season in the Algarve — wineries are especially lively. Book Quinta dos Vales tasting in advance via their website. Silves is a highlight of the Algarve interior — don't miss it. Combined transport + entry costs for the day: ~€15–20.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle from a local shop in Carvoeiro or Lagoa (€10–15/day) and cycle the quiet inland roads through the Algarve countryside. Head toward Alte — a picturesque whitewashed village in the Serra do Caldeirão foothills, known as one of the prettiest villages in the Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Alte village — visit the 16th-century Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Assunção, the natural spring (Fonte Grande), and the scenic picnic area along the stream. Swim in the natural freshwater pools (free). Enjoy the peaceful rural atmosphere far from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Cycle or bus back to the coast. Relax at Praia de Carvoeiro for the golden hour. Watch the sunset from the Algar Seco rock formations just east of Carvoeiro beach — dramatic sea-sculpted limestone pillars and arches, free to visit.

meals.breakfast: Café in Carvoeiro — coffee and tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich) for €3–4
meals.lunch: Snack bar or local café in Alte village — simple grilled chicken or soup for €6–8
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Fonte in Alte (if staying late) OR back in Carvoeiro — try Nah Nah Bah bar for affordable burgers and snacks (€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: The cycle to Alte is approximately 20 km each way — moderate difficulty with some hills. Alternatively, take a local bus to Alte and enjoy the village without cycling. Alte's natural pools are a hidden gem popular with locals. Bring a towel and water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus west to Lagos (45 min from Portimão, ~€3). Explore Lagos old town — walk the historic city walls, visit the Igreja de Santo António (€3 entry, beautiful gilded baroque interior), and browse the colorful local market at Praça Gil Eanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — Lagos' most spectacular coastal landmark. This headland features towering golden sea stacks, grottos, and arches. Take a boat grotto tour from the dock below (€15–20 per person — best value in the Algarve for this experience). Alternatively, walk the cliff paths for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos' lively but affordable evening scene. Walk along Rua 25 de Abril for tapas bars and petiscos (Portuguese tapas). Lagos has a great backpacker-friendly food scene with plenty of budget options.

meals.breakfast: Padaria/bakery in Lagos old town — fresh bread roll, butter, coffee for €2–3
meals.lunch: Mercado de Lagos food stalls — fresh grilled fish, local cheeses, and fruit for €7–9
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Dois Irmãos in Lagos — hearty portions of cataplana (seafood stew) or grilled fish for €10–13; affordable house wine

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is one of the Algarve's most popular towns but remains budget-friendly if you eat where locals eat. Ponta da Piedade boat tours are best in the morning when seas are calmer. Book at the dock or in advance online. Lagos is easily walkable — no need for taxis.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the beaches west of Lagos — take a local bus or taxi to Praia do Camilo (dramatic cliff access via wooden staircase, free) and Praia Dona Ana (beautiful sheltered cove). These are among the most photographed beaches in the Algarve. Swim and explore the sea caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head further west to Sagres (1 hour by bus from Lagos, ~€4) — the southwestern tip of Europe. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — a dramatic clifftop fortress with a giant wind rose and sweeping Atlantic views. Walk to Cabo de São Vicente, the most southwesterly point of continental Europe — a truly spectacular headland.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos or head back toward Lagoa. Sunset at Cabo de São Vicente (if timing allows) is extraordinary — this is one of the best sunsets in all of Portugal. A lighthouse marks the cape where sailors once believed the world ended.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos before departure — galão and pastel de nata (€3)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Sagres fortress or packed lunch from supermarket (€5–7)
meals.dinner: Back in Carvoeiro/Lagoa area — Restaurante O Castelo or another local tasca for grilled fish and house wine (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The bus from Lagos to Sagres runs a few times daily; check Eva/Rede Expressos timetables. Cabo de São Vicente is free to visit. The lighthouse shop sells affordable local honey, liqueurs, and ceramics as souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha. September seas are still warm and the beach is less crowded than summer peak. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) — rentals available locally for €10–15/hour. The calm waters around the rock formations are ideal for beginners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ferragudo — a charming, relatively undiscovered fishing village across the Arade River from Portimão (short ferry crossing or 10-min drive). Explore the whitewashed village, the 16th-century Castelo de São João de Arade (exterior viewing), and the beautiful Praia Grande de Ferragudo.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening at Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa (if not yet visited) or purchase a bottle of local Algarve wine and enjoy it at a cliff-top viewpoint near Praia da Marinha as the sun sets over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local padaria — coffee, juice, toast with local doce de figo (fig jam) for €4–5
meals.lunch: Café/snack bar in Ferragudo village — local seafood sandwich or prego (steak sandwich) for €5–7
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — highly regarded for fresh seafood at reasonable prices; grilled sea bream or prawns for €12–15

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is a wonderful alternative to the more touristy Portimão and Carvoeiro. The ferry from Portimão to Ferragudo is a fun and cheap crossing. September is perfect for SUP — calm seas and warm water. Algarve cooperative wines are excellent value (€3–5 per bottle from the adega).

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus east toward Armação de Pêra (20 min, ~€2). Visit the Nossa Senhora do Rocio chapel perched on the cliff edge, then walk along the long sandy beach — one of the longest in the central Algarve. Quieter than Albufeira, with a more local feel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Albufeira (30 min by bus from Armação de Pêra). Explore Albufeira's historic old town — the original fishing village with whitewashed houses, the Igreja Matriz ruins, and the Praça dos Pescadores. Take the tunnel elevator down to Praia dos Pescadores for a swim.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's Rua Cândido dos Reis (the 'Strip') for affordable bars and restaurants — it's lively but has budget-friendly options. Take the evening bus back to the Lagoa area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local café (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Armação de Pêra beach — fresh grilled fish sandwich or salad for €6–8
meals.dinner: Albufeira old town — Restaurante A Ruína built into cliff ruins overlooking the beach; try the mixed grilled fish for €11–14

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira is more touristy than other Algarve towns but the old town retains authentic charm. Avoid the overpriced beachfront restaurants — the best value is in the old town streets. Bus connections between Armação de Pêra, Albufeira, and Lagoa are reliable and cheap.

day_by_day.morning: Full day excursion east to Faro — the Algarve's capital. Take the bus from Portimão or Albufeira (1–1.5 hrs, €5–7). Explore the Cidade Velha (Old Town) — walk through the Arco da Vila, visit the Gothic Sé Cathedral (€3.50, climb the tower for panoramic views), and stroll the atmospheric cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Igreja dos Ossos (Bone Chapel) in Faro — a small but fascinating ossuary chapel decorated with the bones of monks (€3 entry). Then take a free walk along the Ria Formosa boardwalk and visit the Parque Natural da Ria Formosa visitor center — a vast coastal lagoon system of extraordinary natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Faro's local restaurant scene around Rua do Prior and Rua de Santo António — excellent value compared to coastal tourist towns. Take the evening bus back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at Pastelaria Gardy in Faro — a local institution (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Mercado Municipal de Faro — fresh seafood, local cheeses, and produce at market prices (€6–8)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Ricky in Faro — beloved local restaurant with generous portions of traditional Algarve cuisine for €9–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Faro is often overlooked by tourists but is a genuinely beautiful and authentic Portuguese city. The Ria Formosa is a UNESCO-listed natural park — consider a boat tour of the lagoon and barrier islands (€15–20) if time allows. Faro Airport transfer knowledge is useful for the final day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Monchique — a mountain village in the Serra de Monchique, the highest range in southern Portugal (bus from Portimão, ~1 hr, €3.50). Walk through the eucalyptus and medronho (arbutus) forests. Visit the ruined Convento de Nossa Senhora do Desterro for atmospheric views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or take a short taxi to Fóia — the highest peak in the Algarve at 902m. On a clear September day, you can see all the way to Cape St. Vincent and across to Morocco. Visit the local artisan stalls selling medronho brandy, smoked sausages, and honey — excellent budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Portimão/Lagoa. Stop in Monchique town for a tasting of medronho — the traditional local firewater distilled from arbutus berries (free tastings at most shops). Pick up a small bottle (€5–8) as a souvenir.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or café before departure (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique — hearty mountain food; try presunto serrano (mountain ham), black pork stew, or grilled chouriço for €8–11
meals.dinner: Back in Carvoeiro/Lagoa — light meal at a local café or supermarket provisions (€6–8) after a full day of exploring

day_by_day.notes: Monchique and Fóia offer a completely different landscape from the coastal Algarve — lush, green, and cool. September is ideal for hiking. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The medronho brandy is strong (45%+ ABV) — taste responsibly! Bus from Portimão to Monchique runs ~4 times daily.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day at Praia da Marinha — your home beach for the trip. Arrive early for the best spots. Explore any sea caves or rock formations you haven't yet visited. Take final photos of the dramatic cliffs. Consider hiring a kayak one last time to paddle around the headlands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Algar Seco coastal rock formations near Carvoeiro (free, 10-min walk from Carvoeiro beach). These extraordinary limestone formations have been sculpted by the sea into bridges, arches, and pools. Walk the boardwalk paths and explore the natural swimming pools in the rocks.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Carvoeiro. Splurge slightly on a nicer meal to celebrate the end of the trip. Watch the final sunset from the Carvoeiro clifftop boardwalk — one of the most romantic spots in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy it fully on this relaxed final full day (€4–6 or included)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Marinha or packed picnic from local supermarket (€5–7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — a local favorite for fresh grilled fish and seafood; treat yourself to the fresh catch of the day with a glass of Algarve white wine (€14–18 per person as a slight splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do any final shopping for souvenirs — local almonds, figs, carob products, medronho, and Algarve wine are all great budget-friendly gifts. Pack bags in the evening. Confirm airport transfer or bus schedule for the following morning. September sunsets in the Algarve are spectacular — don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Lagoa Boutique Stay. Arrange transfer to Faro Airport (book shared shuttle in advance for €15–20, or take the bus via Portimão for ~€5–7 total). Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Enjoy one final pastel de nata and galão at the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, cliffs, seafood, and authentic Portuguese culture in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at home.

meals.breakfast: Quick café breakfast at hotel before checkout or at Faro Airport (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Airport café or snacks packed from supermarket the night before (€5–8)
meals.dinner: In-flight or on arrival home

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation): €400–550 per person, covering transport (~€80), food (~€200–250), activities and entry fees (~€80–100), wine tastings (~€30–40), and miscellaneous/souvenirs (~€40–60). This is very achievable with smart choices — eating at local tascas, using public buses, and prioritizing free natural attractions which the Algarve has in abundance.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first walk down to Praia da Marinha, one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches. Explore the golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise water. A short coastal path offers stunning panoramic views — perfect for an easy, relaxed introduction to the region.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the village of Carvoeiro (10 min drive) for a gentle first evening. Walk the boardwalk above Praia de Carvoeiro and watch the sunset over the cliffs before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport or on the road during transfer.
meals.lunch: Light bite at a café near the hotel upon arrival — try a 'tosta mista' (toasted ham and cheese) and a galão (milky espresso).
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — a mid-range local favourite with fresh grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and regional wines. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Pick up a local SIM card or confirm data roaming at the airport. The drive from Faro to Praia da Marinha is straightforward via the A22 motorway.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a proper Portuguese breakfast at a local pastelaria, then head to Praia de Benagil (15 min drive or 20 min coastal walk). Book a kayak or stand-up paddleboard tour to enter the famous Benagil Sea Cave — one of the most spectacular natural formations in Europe. Book in advance as spots fill quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Praia da Marinha for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing. The September sea temperature (~22°C) is ideal. Explore the rock pools and natural arches along the beach at low tide.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the charming village of Lagoa (15 min drive) for an evening stroll through the old town and a visit to the local wine cooperative — Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — which often has tasting sessions in the early evening. Pick up a bottle of local red or white.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Carvoeiro — pastel de nata, fresh orange juice, and a bica (espresso). ~€4–6.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar near Benagil — grilled sardine sandwich or prego (steak roll) with a cold Sagres beer. ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Taberna da Praça in Lagoa — rustic tavern-style restaurant with regional Algarve cuisine. Try arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice). ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Benagil kayak tours should be booked 24–48 hours ahead. Wear water shoes as the cave entry can be rocky. The Lagoa wine cooperative is a great budget-friendly tasting experience — bottles start from €5–8.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west along the coast to Portimão (20 min). Visit the Museu de Portimão, a fascinating free-to-enter museum built inside a former sardine canning factory, detailing the region's fishing and industrial heritage. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha (5 min from Portimão centre) — a wide, golden sandy beach backed by dramatic red cliffs and a 17th-century fortress (Fortaleza de Santa Catarina). Swim, explore the fortress ruins, and enjoy the lively beach atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner. The riverside strip along the Arade River is lined with excellent seafood restaurants — a must is grilled sardines, for which Portimão is famous throughout Portugal.

meals.breakfast: At your boutique hotel or a nearby café — fresh fruit, yogurt, toast with local honey and butter.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a beach bar on Praia da Rocha — grilled fish of the day with salad and chips. ~€15–20.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic on the Portimão riverside — iconic local institution for charcoal-grilled sardines, sea bass, and local Algarve wine. ~€22–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Museu de Portimão is closed on Mondays — check ahead. Parking in Portimão is available near the riverside. September is still peak season so Praia da Rocha will be busy but manageable.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Silves (25 min from hotel) — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Spend the morning visiting the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal, and the adjacent Gothic Cathedral (Sé de Silves).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town on foot — browse the local market (if operating), visit artisan shops, and walk along the Arade River. Then drive to a nearby wine estate: Quinta dos Vales (15 min from Silves) for a scheduled wine tasting tour of their vineyards and cellar. Book in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Carvoeiro/Praia da Marinha area for a quieter evening. Enjoy sunset drinks at a clifftop bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — a charming restaurant in the castle gardens serving local dishes and light lunches. ~€15–20.
meals.dinner: O Leão de Porches in Porches village (10 min from hotel) — beloved local restaurant with traditional Algarvian home-cooking. Try the lamb or pork dishes. ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales wine tours typically cost €15–25 per person including tastings. Silves castle entry is ~€3. Silves is best explored in the morning before midday heat. September afternoons can still reach 28–32°C inland.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated beach morning at Praia de Albandeira, a hidden gem just a short drive from the hotel. Smaller and more secluded than Marinha, it's surrounded by dramatic cliffs and accessible via a short path. Arrive early for the best spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Armação de Pêra (20 min east) — a larger beach town with a long sandy beach. Walk the promenade, visit the small 17th-century chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Navegantes perched on the cliff, and browse the local fish market area.
day_by_day.evening: Book a sunset boat trip along the Algarve coastline from Armação de Pêra or Portimão — many operators offer 2-hour golden-hour cruises past sea caves and grottos. Return for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria near the hotel — croissant, juice, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Praia de Albandeira — pick up local bread, cheese, cured meats, olives, and fruit from a Lagoa supermarket the evening before. ~€10 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Santola in Armação de Pêra — excellent fresh seafood with a terrace view. Try the cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana for two). ~€30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sunset boat trips cost approximately €30–45 per person. Book through your hotel or local agencies in Armação de Pêra. Albandeira beach has no facilities so bring water and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Lagos (35 min west) — one of the Algarve's most beautiful and historic towns. Explore the old walled town: the Fortaleza da Ponta da Bandeira, the Igreja de Santo António (a baroque masterpiece), and the Mercado de Escravos, the site of Europe's first slave market, now a museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Ponta da Piedade — a breathtaking headland of golden rock formations, sea arches, and grottoes. Hire a small boat or kayak from the beach below to explore the caves up close. Alternatively, hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for the evening. The town has a vibrant but relaxed atmosphere with excellent restaurants, wine bars, and a lovely historic centre to wander after dark.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos old town upon arrival — pastel de nata and coffee at a local pastelaria.
meals.lunch: : A Forja restaurant in Lagos — popular mid-range spot with grilled meats and fish, great value. ~€15–22.
meals.dinner: Adega da Marina in Lagos — rustic, atmospheric wine cellar restaurant with regional Portuguese cuisine and a great wine list. ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is about 35 minutes west of Praia da Marinha. Parking is available at the marina. Ponta da Piedade boat tours from the beach below cost ~€10–15 per person for 30-minute trips. The slave market museum entry is ~€3.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Enjoy a slow morning at the hotel — sleep in, have a leisurely breakfast, and take a gentle morning walk along the Praia da Marinha coastal path at your own pace. Enjoy the quieter mid-week atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Porches Pottery (Olaria Algarve) — just 10 minutes from the hotel. This famous studio has been producing traditional hand-painted Algarvian ceramics since 1968. Watch artisans at work and browse the showroom. A wonderful, relaxed cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening at Adega do Cantor, a winery near Guia (20 min drive) co-founded by Cliff Richard. Offers guided tastings and cellar tours in a beautiful estate setting. Book in advance. Return for a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast or nearby café — eggs, toast, fresh fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Porches village — soup, sandwich, and local wine. ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering a tasting menu at a special-occasion price (~€95–120 per person) OR opt for a more casual dinner at Vila Lisa in Porches (~€25–35 per person) for traditional Algarvian cooking.

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally slower-paced as a mid-trip reset. Adega do Cantor wine tours cost approximately €15–25 per person. Porches Pottery is free to visit. If splurging on Bon Bon, reserve weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente (1 hour west) — the southwestern tip of continental Europe and one of the most dramatic landscapes in Portugal. Visit the lighthouse and the windswept cliffs. The views are extraordinary and the sense of standing at 'the end of the world' is unforgettable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fortaleza de Sagres — a massive 16th-century fortress with a giant wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos) etched into the ground. Walk the clifftop paths around the headland. Then drive back via the west coast, stopping at Praia do Amado, a spectacular surfing beach, for a late afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Lagoa. Stop in Mexilhoeira Grande or Portimão for dinner before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early start — grab pastries and coffee from a café before departing, or eat at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Sagres town — Restaurante A Sagres, a simple, good-value local restaurant with fresh fish and seafood. ~€15–20.
meals.dinner: Tasca da Dona Barca in Portimão — a beloved local tasca (tavern) with hearty Portuguese home-cooking and excellent house wine. ~€18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is the furthest day trip in this itinerary — allow 1 hour each way. Start by 9:00am to make the most of the day. Cabo de São Vicente can be very windy even in September — bring a light layer. Entry to Fortaleza de Sagres is ~€3.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Albufeira (30 min). Explore the historic old town — the whitewashed streets, the clifftop church of São Sebastião, and the lively Praça Miguel Bombarda. Browse the morning market and local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip from Albufeira Marina — choose a dolphin watching tour (2–2.5 hours) to spot bottlenose dolphins in their natural habitat in the Atlantic. This is one of the best areas in Europe for dolphin encounters. Return to the marina by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's old town at a leisurely pace as the evening crowd gathers. Enjoy a drink at a rooftop bar before dinner — the old town terrace bars have wonderful sea views at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Café in Albufeira old town upon arrival — fresh orange juice, pastries, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Ruína in Albufeira — a famous local institution built into the cliff face with sea views. Fresh fish and seafood. ~€20–30.
meals.dinner: Adega do Teatro in Albufeira old town — rustic, mid-range restaurant with regional dishes and a good wine selection. ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin watching tours cost approximately €35–45 per person and should be booked in advance. September is an excellent month for dolphin sightings. Albufeira can be touristy but the old town retains genuine charm — avoid the 'Strip' area.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the area around Praia da Marinha more deeply — take the full Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail), a stunning 5.7km coastal walk between Praia de Vale de Centeanes and Praia da Marinha. The trail passes dramatic cliff formations, hidden beaches, and natural arches. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Praia da Marinha after the hike — swim, read, and enjoy the beautiful surroundings. Alternatively, rent a kayak from a local operator to paddle along the base of the cliffs and into sea caves.
day_by_day.evening: Wine and tapas evening in Lagoa town. Visit a local wine bar to taste Lagoa DOC wines — the region produces excellent whites from Arinto grapes and reds from Negra Mole. Pair with local cheeses and charcuterie.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — hotel or café. Bring water and snacks for the trail.
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at a beach restaurant near Carvoeiro — grilled sea bream, salad, and a cold beer. ~€18–25.
meals.dinner: Wine bar dinner in Lagoa — order a selection of petiscos (Portuguese tapas): chouriço assado, queijo da serra, piri piri prawns, and a bottle of local Lagoa white wine. ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is one of the best coastal walks in Europe — wear good shoes and bring sun protection. The trail is linear so you'll need to return the same way or arrange a taxi back. Start early to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Loulé (40 min northeast) — a vibrant inland market town with a beautiful Moorish-influenced covered market (Mercado de Loulé). Arrive by 9:00am when the market is at its liveliest. Browse fresh produce, local honey, almonds, figs, and handmade crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Quinta da Tôr or another local estate near Loulé for an inland wine tasting experience — the Loulé area produces interesting wines from local grape varieties. Alternatively, visit the nearby Alte village (20 min from Loulé), one of the prettiest traditional villages in the Algarve, with a natural spring and whitewashed houses.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area. Enjoy a final relaxed evening at a favourite restaurant discovered earlier in the trip, or try somewhere new in Carvoeiro.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at the Loulé market — buy fresh fruit and local products to take back.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Bica in Loulé — a local favourite with excellent value daily specials (prato do dia). ~€12–18.
meals.dinner: Casa do Povo in Alte village (if visiting) — traditional Algarvian home-cooking in a charming setting. ~€18–25 per person. OR Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro for a return visit.

day_by_day.notes: Loulé market is best on Saturday mornings when it's largest. If visiting on a weekday, it's still excellent but smaller. The drive inland offers a different perspective of the Algarve away from the coast — rolling hills, orange groves, and carob trees.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to a favourite beach from the trip or try Praia de Vale de Centeanes (accessible from the Seven Valleys trail). Spend the morning swimming, snorkelling, and relaxing. September sea conditions are usually calm and warm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and souvenir hunting in Carvoeiro or Lagoa — pick up local ceramics from Porches Pottery, bottles of Lagoa wine, local honey, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos, a traditional Algarve confection), and artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner — celebrate the end of a wonderful trip with a memorable meal. Splurge slightly on a restaurant that showcases the best of Algarvian cuisine and wine.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast — enjoy it fully on the penultimate day.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — keep it light and casual for the last beach day. Fresh fruit, a sandwich, and a cold drink. ~€10–12.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Vila Lisa in Porches — one of the Algarve's most celebrated traditional restaurants, known for its authentic regional recipes and exceptional wine cellar. Book in advance. ~€35–50 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Pack non-essential items this evening to make the final morning easier. Confirm your transfer or rental car return for departure day. Vila Lisa is a legendary Algarve dining institution — an ideal farewell dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a last slow breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Take one last walk down to Praia da Marinha to say goodbye to the cliffs and sea. Check out of the boutique stay and transfer to Faro Airport (~45 min drive) for your departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Allow at least 2 hours before flight time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Homeward bound — with wonderful memories of the Algarve's beaches, sea caves, clifftop sunsets, and local wines.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast — pastel de nata, orange juice, and a bica at a local café. Savour it.
meals.lunch: Light meal at Faro Airport or a café in Faro if time allows before departure.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at home.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00am — confirm with the hotel. The drive from Praia da Marinha to Faro Airport takes approximately 40–50 minutes via the A22. Return your rental car with a full tank of fuel to avoid surcharges. Duty-free at Faro Airport has a good selection of Portuguese wine and ginjinha liqueur for last-minute gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Walk the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a swim among the rock formations.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha Boutique Stay (approx. 45 min). Settle into your luxury suite, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink on the terrace overlooking the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first stroll along the cliffs above Praia da Marinha. The iconic golden limestone arches and turquoise coves are just steps from the hotel. A gentle 30-minute cliff-top walk gives you a breathtaking introduction to the Algarve coastline without overexerting after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium local restaurant such as Restaurante Bon Bon (Michelin-starred, Carvoeiro, ~15 min drive) — known for its creative tasting menus celebrating Algarvian ingredients. Pair with a curated Portuguese wine flight. Return to the hotel for a nightcap on the terrace under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the boutique hotel — charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh bread, and sparkling water or rosé upon arrival
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon, Carvoeiro — Michelin-starred tasting menu with wine pairing (approx. €120–€180 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-booked. Ask the hotel concierge to arrange a chilled bottle of local wine in your room upon arrival. September weather in Algarve is typically warm (24–28°C) with very little rain — ideal conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — Begin the morning with the signature coastal hike along the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos), starting from Praia da Marinha. Marvel at dramatic sea caves, arched rock formations, and hidden grottos. Descend to the beach for a refreshing swim in the crystalline waters. Bring snorkeling gear (available from the hotel) to explore the rich marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, rent a stand-up paddleboard or kayak from a local operator at Praia da Marinha to explore the sea caves and arches from the water. Alternatively, book a private boat tour along the coastline from Benagil, stopping at the famous Benagil Sea Cave — one of Portugal's most spectacular natural wonders (~20 min drive).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the hotel's terrace bar as the sun dips into the Atlantic. Dinner at Restaurante O Alambique in Lagoa — a refined local restaurant celebrated for its fresh seafood, grilled fish, and regional Algarvian cuisine in an intimate setting.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique hotel — fresh pastries, local honey, artisan cheeses, smoked ham, eggs to order, fresh-pressed orange juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch prepared by the hotel — grilled octopus salad, local bread, olives, and chilled white wine enjoyed on the beach
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Alambique, Lagoa — fresh grilled sea bass or cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) with a bottle of Algarve white wine (approx. €60–€90 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Cave boat tour in advance — it is extremely popular in September. Wear reef shoes for the rocky beach at Praia da Marinha. Apply high-SPF sunscreen as September sun remains strong.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Silves (~25 min) — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), one of the best-preserved Moorish fortresses in Portugal. Explore the ramparts, towers, and archaeological museum inside. Wander through the charming historic town, visiting the Gothic Cathedral of Silves and the local market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting experience at Quinta do Barranco Longo or Quinta dos Vales (both near Silves/Lagoa) — two of the Algarve's most acclaimed wineries. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a structured tasting of 5–6 premium Algarvian wines including Negra Mole and Arinto varieties, paired with local charcuterie and cheese.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Lagoa area. Dinner at Restaurante Museu do Frango in Lagoa — renowned for its piri-piri chicken and traditional Portuguese recipes elevated with premium ingredients. Alternatively, opt for a private chef dinner arranged by the hotel on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast with fresh local fruit, yogurt with Algarvian honey, and a selection of pastries including pastel de nata
meals.lunch: Light tapas-style lunch at the winery during the tasting — charcuterie, aged cheeses, olives, and bread paired with wines
meals.dinner: Restaurante Museu do Frango, Lagoa — traditional piri-piri chicken or slow-braised lamb with regional sides and a bottle of Alentejo red wine (approx. €50–€80 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales offers a sculpture garden on the estate — a unique cultural bonus. Book the winery tour at least 48 hours in advance. The hotel concierge can arrange private guided winery visits with a dedicated sommelier.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at Praia de Benagil — one of the most photographed beaches in Europe. Arrive early (before 10:00) to beat the crowds. Take a guided kayak tour into the legendary Benagil Cave, paddling through the cathedral-like sea cave with its natural skylight. The September light inside the cave is extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Armação de Pêra (~20 min west) and board a premium catamaran cruise along the Algarve coast. Sail past sea caves, grottos, and golden cliffs, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in secluded coves. Many luxury charters include onboard drinks, fresh fruit, and a light seafood lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo (~30 min) — a charming fishing village with stunning estuary views. Follow with a full dinner at the same venue, known for its exceptional fresh fish and seafood caught daily by local fishermen.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoked salmon, avocado toast, eggs Benedict, fresh juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Onboard the catamaran — fresh seafood platter, grilled prawns, local bread, and chilled white wine or rosé
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste, Ferragudo — whole grilled sea bream or lobster with roasted vegetables and a premium Portuguese white wine (approx. €70–€100 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter through the hotel concierge for a more exclusive experience. Ferragudo is a hidden gem — explore the cobbled streets and the Ferragudo Castle viewpoint before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Spa morning at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa. Enjoy a signature Algarvian massage using local carob and almond oils, followed by a hydrotherapy session. This is a perfect mid-trip recovery morning. Alternatively, practice sunrise yoga on the cliff-top arranged by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Portimão (~30 min) and visit the Museu de Portimão — an award-winning museum set in a former sardine canning factory that tells the story of the Algarve's fishing heritage. Afterward, stroll the vibrant Portimão marina and browse the boutiques along the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Titanic in Portimão — one of the Algarve's most celebrated fine-dining establishments, known for its sophisticated Portuguese cuisine, impeccable service, and extensive wine list. A true luxury dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Light spa breakfast at the hotel — fresh fruit, granola, yogurt, herbal teas, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Taberna da Praça in Portimão — a refined tapas restaurant near the marina serving petiscos (Portuguese tapas) with local wines
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic, Portimão — tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring dishes like black pork tenderloin, salt cod, and Algarvian desserts (approx. €100–€150 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the spa treatments at least 2 days in advance. The Museu de Portimão is closed on Mondays — Saturday is ideal. Portimão hosts a Formula 1-style motor racing circuit nearby if that interests you.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente (~1 hour drive west) — the dramatic southwestern tip of Europe. Visit the Sagres Fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres), a UNESCO-listed site steeped in the Age of Discovery. Walk to Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse for breathtaking views of the Atlantic where two oceans meet. The September morning light here is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the wild and unspoiled beaches of the Costa Vicentina — Praia do Beliche and Praia do Tonel are stunning surf beaches near Sagres. Enjoy a swim in the cooler, wilder Atlantic waters. Visit the Sagres town center and browse the local artisan shops for handmade ceramics and cork products.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres at Restaurante A Tasca — a beloved local seafood restaurant known for its exceptionally fresh catch, including barnacles (percebes), clams, and grilled tuna. Return to the hotel by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before the early departure — pastries, eggs, cold cuts, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Mum's in Sagres — casual but excellent seafood, including fresh grilled sardines and prawn piri-piri with local beer or white wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Tasca, Sagres — barnacles, clam cataplana, and grilled tuna with a crisp Vinho Verde (approx. €50–€75 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start early (depart by 9:00) to make the most of the day. The drive along the Costa Vicentina is scenic and worth taking the coastal road (N268). Bring a light jacket — Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September.

day_by_day.morning: Private wine tasting masterclass at Adega do Cantor (near Guia, ~30 min) — the winery owned by Sir Cliff Richard, producing award-winning Vida Nova wines. Enjoy a private guided tour of the estate, vineyards, and cellar, followed by an exclusive tasting of their premium red, white, and rosé wines with a sommelier.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery visit, head to Carvoeiro (~20 min) — a picturesque fishing village turned upscale resort town. Explore the charming main beach, the colorful cliff-top boardwalk of Algar Seco (a stunning rock formation with natural pools), and the boutique shops along the village streets.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at Restaurante O Castelo, Carvoeiro — perched on the clifftop with panoramic ocean views. Dinner at Restaurante Laranjeira in Carvoeiro — an elegant restaurant offering a refined menu of Portuguese and Mediterranean cuisine with an exceptional wine list.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with regional specialties including almond cake and carob jam
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café in Carvoeiro — fresh prawn salad, bruschetta with local tomatoes, and a glass of chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Restaurante Laranjeira, Carvoeiro — duck rice, grilled black pork, or fresh turbot with a premium Dão red wine (approx. €65–€95 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor requires advance booking — contact them directly or through the hotel concierge. Algar Seco is best visited in the afternoon when the light catches the rock formations beautifully. Wear comfortable shoes for the boardwalk.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia da Marinha — your home beach. Arrive early to secure the best spot on this stunning but compact beach. Spend the morning swimming, sunbathing, and snorkeling among the sea caves and rock arches. The water clarity in September is exceptional.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided jeep safari through the Algarve hinterland — explore the rugged Serra do Caldeirão mountains, traditional whitewashed villages, cork oak forests, and carob orchards. Visit a local family farm to see traditional Algarvian food production (honey, cheese, figs, almonds). Many premium operators offer this as a half-day experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Henrique Leis in Almancil (~40 min) — one of Portugal's most celebrated Michelin-starred restaurants, run by Swiss-born chef Henrique Leis. The menu blends European technique with Algarvian ingredients in a beautifully designed space.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs any style, fresh orange juice, local pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the mountains during the jeep safari — prepared by the hotel with local bread, cheese, charcuterie, fruit, and local wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Henrique Leis, Almancil — Michelin-starred tasting menu with wine pairing (approx. €150–€200 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the jeep safari through a premium operator such as Jeep Safari Algarve or Zoomarine Safaris. The drive to Almancil for dinner is worth every minute — book the restaurant well in advance as it is consistently full in September.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Loulé (~40 min) — the cultural heart of the Algarve. Visit the spectacular Mercado de Loulé, a Moorish-style market hall filled with fresh produce, spices, local cheeses, honey, and handcrafts. Explore the Loulé Castle and the charming historic center with its traditional craft workshops (copper work, leather, and ceramics).
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting at Quinta da Tôr near Loulé — a boutique organic winery producing elegant Algarvian wines in a beautiful rural setting. Enjoy a guided vineyard walk and cellar tour followed by a tasting of their organic wines paired with local snacks. The estate views over the rolling countryside are superb.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Aux Deux Sardines in Loulé — a refined French-Portuguese fusion restaurant in the heart of the old town, known for its creative seasonal menu and outstanding wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh fruit platter, granola, yogurt, and pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Calcinha in Loulé market — a legendary local institution serving traditional Algarvian dishes including açorda de marisco (seafood bread soup) and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Restaurante Aux Deux Sardines, Loulé — seasonal tasting menu with French-Portuguese influences and premium wine pairing (approx. €80–€120 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Loulé market is most vibrant on Saturday mornings — if you can adjust, consider swapping this day. Quinta da Tôr requires advance booking. Pick up local artisan products at the market as gifts or for your hotel room.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise paddleboard session at Praia da Marinha — arranged through the hotel. The early morning sea is typically glassy and calm in September, making for a magical experience on the water as the sun rises over the cliffs. Follow with a cliff-top yoga session if offered by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro (~50 min) — the Algarve's elegant capital. Visit the Cidade Velha (Old Town) within the ancient city walls, the stunning Gothic Cathedral (Sé de Faro) with its rooftop terrace offering panoramic views, and the fascinating Museu Municipal de Faro. Explore the charming pedestrian streets and boutique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Faz Gostos in Faro — a beautifully restored historic building in the old town serving refined modern Portuguese cuisine. Known for its innovative approach to traditional Algarvian flavors and exceptional local wine list.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-activity breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, and a coffee before the paddleboard session, followed by the full hotel breakfast after
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Gardy in Faro — a classic Faro institution near the marina, serving excellent fresh fish and seafood in a refined setting
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos, Faro — modern Portuguese tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring Algarvian tuna, black pork, and seasonal vegetables (approx. €75–€110 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Faro Cathedral rooftop offers one of the best views in the Algarve — go up in the late afternoon for golden hour light. The Ria Formosa Natural Park boardwalk near Faro is worth a short walk before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat trip to the Ria Formosa Natural Park from Faro or Olhão (~50 min drive). Explore this stunning coastal lagoon system — a UNESCO-protected area — by private boat, visiting the barrier islands of Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) and Ilha do Farol. Swim in the warm, shallow lagoon waters and walk the pristine white sand beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tavira (~1 hour drive east) — arguably the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the hilltop castle with its stunning views, the Igreja de Santa Maria do Castelo, and the charming cobbled streets lined with azulejo-tiled buildings. Browse the artisan shops and local galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Quatro Águas in Tavira — a legendary seafood restaurant on the Gilão River estuary, known for its exceptional cataplana de marisco and fresh grilled fish with river and castle views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with regional specialties
meals.lunch: Lunch on Ilha Deserta at Restaurante Estamine — the only restaurant on the desert island, serving fresh seafood and salads with feet in the sand (seasonal — confirm availability)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Quatro Águas, Tavira — cataplana de marisco, grilled sole, and local Tavira wine (approx. €65–€95 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat to Ria Formosa well in advance. Ilha Deserta is one of the most serene spots in Portugal — bring a good book and sunscreen. The drive from Faro to Tavira along the EN125 passes through charming villages worth a brief stop.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Lagoa/Carvoeiro area for a premium golf morning at Amendoeira Golf Resort or Pestana Golf Resort (~20–30 min drive) — two of the Algarve's finest golf courses with stunning ocean and countryside views. Even if golf is not your primary interest, the courses offer a quintessential Algarve luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon at Praia da Marinha — your beloved home beach. Spend a leisurely few hours swimming, snorkeling, and soaking up the last of the Algarve sun. Rent a kayak for one final exploration of the sea caves. Visit the hotel spa for a relaxing facial or massage to prepare for the journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest restaurant of your trip — Restaurante Vila Joya in Albufeira (~30 min drive) — a legendary two-Michelin-starred restaurant considered one of the best in Portugal. Chef Dieter Koschina creates extraordinary tasting menus inspired by the Algarve's finest ingredients. Book months in advance.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory hotel breakfast — full gourmet spread with a glass of sparkling wine to mark the penultimate day
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel pool or beach — fresh salads, grilled prawns, and a bottle of chilled Algarve rosé
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vila Joya, Albufeira — two-Michelin-starred tasting menu with premium wine pairing (approx. €200–€280 per person). One of Portugal's greatest dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Vila Joya must be booked months in advance — do this before your trip. The restaurant is inside a boutique hotel and has extremely limited covers. Dress code is smart elegant. This is the culinary highlight of the entire trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel. Take one last cliff-top walk above Praia da Marinha to say goodbye to the golden limestone arches and turquoise sea. Pack and check out. Visit the local Lagoa market (open Sunday mornings) to pick up final souvenirs — local wines, almond sweets, carob products, and handmade ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final lunch in the Lagoa or Carvoeiro area before your private transfer to Faro Airport. If time allows, stop at a local pastelaria for a final pastel de nata and coffee — a perfect farewell to Portugal.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve — the golden cliffs, the crystalline sea, the world-class wines, and the exceptional Portuguese hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet hotel breakfast — order everything you loved most during the stay. Savor it slowly.
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Alcaide in Lagoa — a beloved local spot serving traditional Algarvian cuisine including grilled fish, black pork, and regional desserts with a glass of local wine for a perfect farewell meal (approx. €40–€60 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for the transfer and check-in at Faro Airport. Ask the hotel to prepare a farewell gift bag with local products — many boutique hotels do this for departing guests. Confirm your private transfer the night before. Obrigado e boa viagem!
